source.title: Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay.

confidence_rationale: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity, as ARC-121 is an architectural framing claim. The paper's explicit stated contribution is that planning, learning and consolidation are not separate functions but one prioritized-access operation over one common value/model representation -- that is ARC-121's thesis instantiated at exactly three of the consumers ARC-121 names. Held below 0.8 because the shared object demonstrated is a value/successor structure over a spatial MDP, materially narrower than the knowledge/belief/uncertainty/possibility/commitment bundle ARC-121 asserts, and because the evidence is a normative model fitted to existing place-cell findings rather than a decisive new measurement.
failure_signatures: The unification is demonstrated over a single spatial-navigation MDP; the paper does not show that the same prioritized-access quantity governs access to non-spatial, ethical or self-model content, so convergence outside that domain is asserted by extension rather than measured.

A single normative rule explaining several phenomena is compatible with those phenomena being implemented by separate mechanisms that happen to approximate the same optimum; the paper's evidence is behavioural/statistical fit, not a demonstration that one physical representation is read by all three functions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A normative theory in which memories are accessed in order of the utility of accessing them (gain x need) predicts hippocampal replay statistics and 'unifies seemingly disparate proposed functions of replay including planning, learning, and consolidation'.
mapping.ree_translation: Replay, planning and learning in REE should not be built as three mechanisms with private state; they are three read/update patterns over one shared epistemic-state object, differing in which access-priority regime is active rather than in what they operate on. Directly supports ARC-121's core assertion for the prediction/replay/planning/learning subset of consumers.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The shared object in the paper is a value function plus a transition model over a small spatial MDP. ARC-121's object additionally spans possibility, commitment and harm/ethics evaluation; this paper speaks to NONE of the ethics/harm consumer, and the extension from a spatial value structure to a general epistemic relationship is REE's inference, not the authors'.
mapping.source_context: Simulated rodent spatial navigation tasks, compared against published hippocampal place-cell replay statistics (forward/reverse replay, reward modulation, novelty effects).

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Nature Neuroscience; theory reproduces a broad, independently collected body of replay findings). Mapping fidelity is the highest in this pull because the paper's own framing is unification-of-functions-over-one-representation. Transfer risk is moderate rather than low: spatial-MDP to general epistemic state is a real leap.
